title: Measuring Mitochondrial Respiration in Human Adipocytes Using Seahorse XF Analyzer
author: Broghammer, Gebhardt, et al.
materials: Seahorse XF Cell Mito Stress Test Kit
Seahorse XFe96 Pro Extracellular Flux Assay Kit
Timing: Any time after the assay

steps.title: Prepare dissociation buffer
steps.instruction: Add 0.2 % collagenase type II to the dissociation buffer and pre‑warm the buffer to 37 °C in a water bath.

steps.title: Mince adipose tissue
steps.instruction: Hold the adipose tissue firmly with forceps, scrape it away from surrounding connective tissue with a spoon‑shaped spatula, and cut the tissue into pieces of approximately 1–3 mm³ using scissors.

steps.title: Digest tissue in buffer
steps.instruction: Place the minced tissue in a 50 mL tube, add pre‑warmed dissociation buffer to achieve a tissue‑to‑buffer ratio of ~1.5 : 1 (e.g., 30 mL tissue + 20 mL buffer), close the tube tightly and incubate in a 37 °C water bath for 30–45 min, inverting the tube gently every 5–10 min (do not exceed 50 min).

steps.title: Filter cell suspension
steps.instruction: Remove the tube from the water bath and filter the suspension through a heat‑sterilized stainless‑steel tea strainer, then attach a 21‑gauge blunt‑end cannula to a 20 mL syringe, draw the solution up and filter it through a 300 µm syringe strainer.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect adipocytes
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the filtered suspension at 100 × g at 20–25 °C for 2 min; adipocytes will float on top. Insert a syringe needle into the 50 mL tube and remove the infranatant containing dissociation buffer and stromal vascular fraction.

steps.title: Wash adipocytes repeatedly
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL wash buffer, invert the tube gently 8–10 times, and centrifuge again at 100 × g at 20–25 °C for 2 min. Remove the infranatant and repeat the washing step until a densely packed adipocyte fraction is obtained, discarding any top lipid layer that appears after several washes.

steps.title: Rest and prepare culture plates
steps.instruction: Let the packed adipocyte fraction rest at 20–25 °C for ~15 min while you prepare a 6‑well cell‑culture plate and 0.4 µm transwell inserts.

steps.title: Add medium to wells
steps.instruction: Pipette 4 mL culture medium (CM) into each well of the 6‑well plate.

steps.title: Prepare transwell inserts
steps.instruction: Remove the transwell inserts from their packaging, place them upside down on the sterile workbench, and use a gloved thumb to make a small indentation in each membrane.

steps.title: Seed adipocytes onto membranes
steps.instruction: Pipette 300–750 µL of the adipocyte suspension onto each membrane, quickly invert the transwell and place it into a prepared well containing CM.

steps.title: Add medium to inner well
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL CM to the inner well of each transwell.

steps.title: Incubate cultures
steps.instruction: Place the plate lid on the plate and transfer it to a humidified incubator set to 37 °C with 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Perform medium exchanges
steps.instruction: For experiments using different or supplemented CM, exchange the medium every other day, taking care not to aspirate the adipocytes.

steps.title: Optional culture duration
steps.instruction: Mature adipocytes can be cultured in MAACs for up to 14 days while maintaining viability; OCR measurements are recommended after at least one day post‑isolation.

steps.title: Open data in Wave software
steps.instruction: Open your experiment in the Seahorse XF Wave desktop software.

steps.title: Normalize to cell area
steps.instruction: Normalize the data for the area covered by cells, as calculated from the assay images.

steps.title: Exclude outliers
steps.instruction: Use the Seahorse XF Wave software to detect and exclude possible outlier wells.

steps.title: Export report
steps.instruction: Export the data as a Seahorse XF Cell Mito Stress Test Report using the Report Generator.

steps.title: Analyze parameters and plot
steps.instruction: Export raw kinetic data to Excel or GraphPad, calculate basal respiration, maximal respiration, proton leak, ATP synthesis, and spare respiratory capacity according to the manufacturer’s instructions, and plot the results. Optionally analyze ECAR for additional metabolic insight.

description: The Seahorse extracellular flux technology enables the real-time measurement of mitochondrial respiration in adherent cell types and tissue explants. However, applying this technology freshly isolated mature adipocytes has been technically challenging, as they are difficult to attach securely to the bottom of the well due to their high lipid content and buoyancy. Consequently, pioneering work and protocols have relied on stromal vascular fraction (SVF)-derived adipocytes that are differentiated in vitro, or on bulk adipose tissue/explant preparations that contain multiple non-adipocyte cell types.1 An oxygraph system has been used to perform high-resolution respirometry on human mature adipocytes,2 allowing a detailed evaluation of mitochondrial respiratory capacity under specific substrate conditions. However, it does not provide the multiplexed, higher-throughput measurements possible with the Seahorse platform, such as simultaneous measurements of oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR).
